emails.body:
Hi [First Name],

We work with a regional brand very similar to yours that recently moved from static to digital menu boards.

Would you be interested in seeing the results they got?

Sales: what happened to average check and featured items
ROI: how quickly it paid for itself, including print savings
Setup: how we made it simple to set up and test in a few stores first

Happy to walk you through it in a quick 15-minute call, or send a short summary first if that’s easier.

Best,
Michael Mathieu
Vistify

Hi [First Name],

We’d like to send you a free, shop-level revenue analysis comparing Dutch Bros’ current printed drive-thru boards with digital boards.

The short version:

Digital menu boards typically lift the average check 2–6% (Forrester).
At ~$2.1M per shop, even 2% is about $42,000 per shop, per year.
Across 1,000+ shops, that’s $42M+, before any print and labor savings.

With a drink menu that changes as often as yours, the boards can also feature seasonal drinks and limited-time offers by time of day, with no reprints.

Would you like to schedule a quick call to walk you through how digital menus could lift you overall sales rather signficantly?

Best,
Michael Mathieu
Vistify

Hi [First Name],

Congratulations on bringing Toast across your 200+ shops this year. It's a big lift, and it opens up something useful on the menu board side.

Vistify's vMenu syncs directly with Toast, so items, prices, modifiers and sold-out status flow straight to in-store screens with no double entry. From recent store photos, most Teriyaki Madness locations still run printed panels, which means every price change or new bowl becomes a reprint-and-ship project.

We've put together a short brief for you: a mockup of your current menu running on vMenu, plus a simple model of what printed updates cost across the system today.

Would you be open to a 30-minute call to walk through it? Happy to work around your calendar.

Best,
Michael Mathieu
Vistify

Hi [First Name],

Andy's runs one of the best seasonal calendars in frozen treats with dynamic changes.  

How do you keep your customers up to speed with all thje new menu items to max awareness and revenue?

That's what my company Vistify specializes in--we help chains like yours change menus, prices and seasonal features across every location in minutes, synced to the POS, so a new LTO goes live the morning it launches instead of when the panels arrive.

In your 40th year, we thought it might be useful to show you what that could look like. We've prepared a short brief with a mockup of an Andy's board on vMenu and a rough look at annual reprint costs at your scale.

Could we find 30 minute in the next couple of weeks?

Best,
Michael Mathieu
Vistify

sections.heading: How these were checked
lines: For each chain, we reviewed Google Images results for its menu boards, filtered to images indexed in the past year, typically 15–25 photos spanning multiple locations, and judged whether the boards are printed panels or screens.
Note: the past-year filter reflects when Google indexed the image, not exactly when it was taken, so a few photos may be older.

sections.heading: Verdicts
lines: Static — printed or backlit panels in essentially every recent photo.
Mostly static — printed panels in most photos; one or two stores show a screen.
Mixed — a meaningful share of stores show screens (often newer builds or interiors); best approached store-by-store or via the drive-thru.

sections.heading: Notes
lines: The list includes larger chains (Jersey Mike's, Jimmy John's, Dutch Bros, Rita's, Cook Out, In-N-Out), so it is no longer limited to 50–250 units.
'Sale difficulty' is a judgment on how hard the account is likely to be for Vistify, not a finding from the photos.
Unit counts marked approximate should be re-verified before outreach.
Next step: map decision-makers (CMO, COO, VP Ops, VP Technology, franchise development) for the top accounts.
